svg.title: IceCube: a cubic kilometre of ice, roughly to scale
svg.desc: A drawing of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole, seen from slightly above. A hexagon of vertical strings hangs in the ice below the surface. Light sensors sit on the strings between 1,450 metres and 2,450 metres deep, filling a hexagonal block about 1 kilometre across and 1 kilometre tall: a cubic kilometre of ice. In all there are 5,160 sensors on 86 strings, in holes drilled into the ice on a hexagonal grid 125 metres apart. On the surface, IceTop has 81 stations on top of the strings. Depth and width are drawn roughly to scale; only some strings and sensors are drawn, and the sensors are drawn far larger than they are. Numbers from the IceCube Collaboration, https://icecube.wisc.edu/science/icecube/ (checked 2026-10-06).

g.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
